text.title: map-reduce-send-fanout Core Rules
text.summary: Migrated testable rules for map-reduce-send-fanout. Verify and refine before relying on for production.

rule.statement: Use map-reduce fan-out (Send / ParallelAgent / asyncio.gather) only when (a) per-item work is independent, (b) every branch is idempotent and retryable, (c) the target state field has a reducer annotation, and (d) concurrency is capped at ≤20.
rule.rationale: LangGraph super-steps fail atomically — one branch crashing reverts the whole step's writes. Without idempotency, retry double-applies side effects. Without a reducer, parallel writes to the same key clobber each other. Above 20 concurrent calls, most providers' rate limits kick in and tail latency dominates the parallelism win.

rule.statement: When the profile is valid, item_count is high-tier (above 20, the r1 concurrency cap, so the list cannot complete in one wave) and mutates_shared_state is advanced — branches write to a shared sink that is not the reduced state field, the fm-04 case of a module-global logger, metrics counter or cache, as opposed to shared business state which is a Skip-If — the fanout-spec MUST enumerate every shared sink, give each branch its own structured logger keyed by item_id that flushes at branch end, and route every other cross-branch write through the reducer field (Annotated[list, operator.add] or an explicit merge). idempotency_guarantee MUST be an idempotency-key store keyed by item_id so a retried super-step re-applies nothing (fm-02), max_attempts MUST be explicit and counted per super-step, not per branch, and concurrency_cap MUST stay at or below 20 with the remainder of the list scheduled in further waves. audit.rule_refs cites r1.

rationale.source: LangGraph documentation (Send API, reducers, super-step semantics); failure modes fm-02 and fm-04 of this methodology

rule.rationale: A LangGraph super-step commits or reverts all branch writes together, so any write that escapes the reducer — a log line, a counter, a cache entry — is applied once per attempt and never rolled back. Naming the sinks and keying side effects by item_id is what makes a retry safe; without it the fan-out is correct on the happy path and double-applies on the first rate-limit error.

rule.statement: When the profile is valid, item_count is high-tier (above 20, the r1 concurrency cap) and mutates_shared_state is not advanced (branches are pure: same input, same output, no writes outside the returned state), the fanout-spec MUST set concurrency_cap in the 8-20 band (fm-01), enforce it with asyncio.Semaphore for plain asyncio or by slicing the Send list per super-step for LangGraph, and state how the remainder beyond one wave is scheduled, because the reference router only emits the first MAX_FANOUT items. reducer MUST be Annotated[list, operator.add] or an explicit merge that preserves item count (fm-03), idempotency_guarantee MUST be declared as pure-branch, max_attempts MUST be explicit, and the record MUST list the item_ids of failed branches rather than returning a shorter list. audit.rule_refs cites r1.

rationale.source: LangGraph documentation (Send API and map-reduce branches); Python asyncio documentation (Semaphore); failure modes fm-01 and fm-03 of this methodology

rule.rationale: Above the cap the semaphore is what actually shapes traffic, and fm-01's 60-way gather shows what happens when it is missing: every branch fails at once at the provider's rate limit. The count-preserving reducer and the explicit failed-item list are the two checks that turn a silent partial result into a visible one, which is the whole point of an atomic super-step.

rule.statement: When the profile is valid and item_count is low-tier — at least 3 (the Skip-If floor) and at most 20 (the r1 cap), so the whole list fits in one wave — the fanout-spec MUST set concurrency_cap equal to item_count, use the framework's native primitive (LangGraph Send, ADK ParallelAgent, or asyncio.gather under a Semaphore for plain Python) with no wave scheduling, keep reducer as Annotated[list, operator.add] or an explicit merge (fm-03), declare idempotency_guarantee as pure-branch, and set max_attempts explicitly. Adding an idempotency-key store or per-branch loggers on this tier requires a rejected-alternatives entry naming the driver that forced it. audit.rule_refs cites r1.

rationale.source: LangGraph documentation (Send API, reducers); Google ADK documentation (ParallelAgent); rule r1 of this methodology

rule.rationale: Under 20 items every branch can be in flight at once without touching the rate-limit cliff, so wave scheduling and idempotency stores are machinery for a problem this tier does not have. The reducer stays mandatory because fm-03's silent overwrite loses items at 10 exactly as it does at 1000.
